## 1. The reader's question

**Asked:** Not asked: the author asked Claude to write out all the cards on the states of Data Hub, to review them together.

**Answer:** Claude's suggestion, from the places that meet the reader (MSG-KEY-01 "An Excel key expires within a month" and MSG-KEY-02 "The Data Team revoked an Excel key"): "My Excel gets nothing new since this morning. Did someone delete the data?", from a colleague from finance at the month end. Whether colleagues say it this way is for the test reader.

**In the card:** Why now, the quote and the situation.

## 2. What went wrong

**Asked:** Not asked: drafted by Claude.

**Answer:** Claude's suggestion, from DEC-DH-79 (the Excel key: personal, made on My page, shown once, lasts a year, stops when its User can no longer sign in, revoked by the Data Team), DEC-CH-03 (Excel gets only the result of a Lens, its Parameters at their defaults, at every refresh) and the two Messages: the finance team refreshes a Lens through Power Query; a month before its key stops, its User gets the Message, makes a new key on My page and puts it in Excel in the place of the old one. Expected misconceptions, none heard yet: the data was deleted; a new copy of the workbook helps; I share my key with a colleague; a whole Resource can go to Excel.

**In the card:** the situation of Why now; Core idea, "At Immoscoop"; the wrong answers of the three questions.

## 3. The aha

**Asked:** Not asked: drafted by Claude.

**Answer:** Claude's suggestion: Excel gets the result of a Lens through a personal key that lasts a year: when Excel gets nothing new, the key stopped, not the data.

**In the card:** Core idea, the rule.

## 5. Never again, ask first

**Asked:** Not asked: drafted by Claude.

**Answer:** Claude's suggestion: never share your key; a colleague makes their own; ask first "Is my key still valid?". Tested out loud: either answer leads to a next step, not to a wrong one.

**In the card:** You can now, the first question; a wrong answer.

## The ladder

1. **Story:** a key card of a building that stops working after a year: the building is still there.
2. **Structure:** Excel → the Excel key → the Lens → its result, at every refresh; the key stops: Excel gets nothing.
3. **Data Hub:** the Excel keys on My page, and the Message a month before a key stops.

The card has no See it: the third rung is a screen of Data Hub, not a chart. Apply leads there instead. The first two rungs are pictures (Figma work); the card has no place for them yet.

## Who brought what

The author asked Claude to write out all the cards on the states of Data Hub, without an anchor, and reviews them together. Claude brought everything in the card, from the rules of Data Hub and its Messages. A "yes" to a suggestion weighs less than the author's own words, so the fact check and the test reader carry more weight here than usual.

The author reviewed the cards together: "All good", and asked Claude to check the open facts itself. Checked by Claude in the code on 2026-11-14, at the author's request: My page lists every key with its columns Last used and Expires (the texts of the web app); a key signs in in the name of its User (the Excel key in docs/definitions.md), and a change of Permission group holds in Excel too (MSG-USR-01). The card says both.
